Lori is present throughout the relevant scenarios, so she directly knows what Teresa says and does in their conversations. By scenario 3, Lori knows Teresa is hesitant about seeing a career counselor and has expressed doubt about whether it will help. Lori’s intent there is to convince Teresa that professional advice/career counseling is worthwhile.

By scenario 4, Lori organizes a meeting with Jamie, who successfully changed careers, specifically hoping to inspire Teresa. At this point, Teresa says she is afraid of making the wrong decision, so Lori’s intent shifts toward helping Teresa overcome her fear of change by using Jamie’s example.

Lori does not know Teresa’s private unspoken thoughts beyond what Teresa expresses, nor does she yet know whether Teresa will ultimately attend counseling until scenario 5. She also does not know future outcomes or the counselor’s perspective at the time of scenarios 3–4.

Thus, Lori’s intention changes from convincing Teresa of the benefits of professional advice to helping Teresa overcome her fear of change.
